sections.h2: Which Scotland County office holds the land records?
sections.html:
Land records for Scotland County sit with its Register of Deeds, which describes itself as custodian of deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, plats and other legal papers. The same staff issue birth and death certificates and marriage licenses, and they file military discharges.

A home sale there ends with the buyer's deed landing in this office. The county's page for the department keeps the research tools in one spot, so a seller can read the public trail on a parcel before any offer arrives.

sections.h2: What search tools does Scotland County offer for deeds and plats?
sections.html:
The county splits its tools by era and by purpose:

  • One index covers 1978 to the present together with every plat, and you enter it by signing in as a guest.
  • A second search holds pre-1978 documents at a new web address.
  • The Laurinburg and Scotland County GIS map often shows an owner's name and usually a book and page cite for the deed.
  • A tax foreclosure listing is reachable from the department page, where you scroll to the Scotland County entries.
  • PropertyCheck lets you save names and receive a notice when a filing appears.

For rights of way from before 1978, the office asks you to email the references. Bring book and page numbers if you are chasing an old easement across a lot.

sections.h2: What does Scotland County check before accepting a deed?
sections.html:
The recorder reviews each instrument against statutory prerequisites and the state's Document Standards. The county lists the usual ones:

  • Papers are normally originals bearing original signatures and proof of notarization.
  • A North Carolina deed or deed of trust names its drafter, a person or a law firm, on page one.
  • Fees are collected before filing, unless a statute lets the paper be recorded free.
  • A transfer of real property, other than a mortgage or deed of trust, must state the excise tax owed by the grantor.

Staff may not practice law, so they cannot help prepare a deed or discuss its legal meaning. Take drafting questions to an attorney.

sections.h2: Can unpaid taxes keep a deed out of the Scotland County records?
sections.html:
They can. The county says that since July 1, 2020, a deed moving real property is turned away unless the Scotland County tax collector has certified that no delinquent county, municipal or other collector-charged taxes are a lien on the land.

An alternative wording is allowed. The deed may carry a line saying a licensed North Carolina attorney prepared it and that any delinquent taxes will be paid to the collector by the closing attorney when closing money is disbursed. That clause is why local closings tend to route through an attorney's trust account.

Before listing, ask the collector for a payoff on each parcel. Tax foreclosures for the county appear in the listing the register of deeds links to.

sections.h2: What do deed recording and excise tax cost in Scotland County?
sections.html:
Recording charges follow the statewide schedule in section 161-10. The excise tax line comes from the Scotland County page.

Charges tied to a deed filed in Scotland County
ItemPrinted figureSource
Standard instrument$26.00 for up to 15 pages, $4.00 per page beyondSection 161-10
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 for up to 35 pages, $4.00 per page beyondSection 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellationFreeSection 161-10
Plat$21.00 per sheetSection 161-10
Excise tax on a deed$2 per $1000, owed by the grantorScotland County page

The county page names several transfers that owe no excise tax: gifts, intestacy, a lease for a term of years, a merger or consolidation, operation of law, and transfers under a will. State statute states the rate as one dollar per $500, which works out to the same $2 per $1000 (section 105-228.30).

sections.h2: What privacy rules apply to documents filed in Scotland County?
sections.html:
Once a paper is recorded in the real property books it becomes a public record that anyone may inspect and copy. Because the county posts images online, it warns filers not to include Social Security, taxpayer ID, driver license, passport, bank account or card numbers, or PIN codes, unless a law or court order requires it or all but the last four digits are redacted.

Anyone can ask in writing to have such data removed from an online image. The request must name the information, identify the document, and say where in the document it appears. The county says no fee is charged for a redaction request, and a person who requests a redaction without authority commits an infraction punishable by a fine up to $500 per violation.

If you are selling and spot your own account number on an old filing, send that written request through the register of deeds.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter when a Scotland County house sells?
sections.html:
A deed or lease running more than three years binds lien creditors and later buyers for value only from the time it is registered in the county where the land sits, and priority follows the order of registration (section 47-18).

That makes same-day filing of the buyer's deed and the lender's deed of trust the normal practice. On the seller's side, a payoff should be followed by a recorded satisfaction, which carries no fee. Keep the recorded deed's book and page numbers with your files, and ask the office to correct the index if a number looks wrong.

sections.h2: Does the Scotland County office handle marriage licenses and vital records?
sections.html:
Yes. Applicants complete a county form and then call 910-277-2575 to schedule an appointment. The county says a license is not valid until signed by the applicants and by staff in the office, lasts 60 days, and covers marriages in North Carolina only.

Birth and death certificates and marriage licenses can be picked up after a call ahead, or ordered by mail through an online request that the county says it processes the day received. Heirs settling a house often need a certified death certificate for the clerk of court, so order extras early.

faqs.q: Can I search Scotland County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes. One index covers 1978 to the present plus all plats, entered by signing in as a guest, and another covers older documents. The GIS map helps when the owner's name is unknown.

faqs.q: What excise tax does a Scotland County deed carry?
faqs.a: The county page prints $2 per $1000, owed by the grantor, matching the state rate of one dollar per $500. Gifts, intestacy and transfers under a will are among the exempt transfers it lists.

faqs.q: Does Scotland County need proof of paid taxes to record a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Since July 1, 2020, a real property deed needs the tax collector's certificate of no delinquent taxes, or an attorney's statement that back taxes will be paid from closing funds.

faqs.q: Will the Scotland County register of deeds draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office is barred from practicing law and cannot help prepare documents. An attorney should draft it and be named on the first page as preparer.

faqs.q: How do I schedule a marriage license in Scotland County?
faqs.a: Fill out the county's form, then call 910-277-2575 for an appointment. The license is good for 60 days and only for marriages held in North Carolina.
